```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE)
r <- readRDS(params$results_rds)
if (inherits(r, "PopgenVCFAnalysis")) {
  a <- r
  r <- c(
    list(
      metadata = a$samples$metadata,
      qc_snps = a$variants$qc_ids,
      final_snps = a$variants$ld_ids,
      qc = a$variants$reports,
      package_version = a$package_version,
      messages = a$messages
    ),
    a$results
  )
}
report_figures <- params$figures
html_escape <- function(x) {
  x <- gsub("&", "&amp;", x, fixed = TRUE)
  x <- gsub("<", "&lt;", x, fixed = TRUE)
  x <- gsub(">", "&gt;", x, fixed = TRUE)
  x <- gsub('"', "&quot;", x, fixed = TRUE)
  x
}
# kable(..., longtable = TRUE) alone does not repeat its header on later
# pages (that needs \endfirsthead/\endhead, which base knitr's longtable
# support doesn't add) -- inserted here by hand at the one \midrule that
# always immediately follows the single header row kable() emits, valid
# minimal longtable syntax (everything above \endhead repeats as the page
# header; omitting \endfirsthead just reuses it for the first page too).
report_kable_repeat_header <- function(rendered) {
  lines <- strsplit(rendered, "\n", fixed = TRUE)[[1L]]
  idx <- which(lines == "\\midrule")[1L]
  if (is.na(idx)) return(rendered)
  paste(append(lines, "\\endhead", after = idx), collapse = "\n")
}

# A long free-text column (e.g. a pipeline-notice message) forced every
# other column in the same row down to an illegibly tiny \resizebox scale on
# a real production report -- confirmed directly. LaTeX tabular/longtable
# cells never wrap on their own; kable() has already produced correctly
# escaped, correctly rounded cell text by this point, so this only performs
# a surgical column-position substitution on kable()'s own trusted data-row
# lines (between the \endhead inserted above and \bottomrule), wrapping each
# long column's already-escaped content in \parbox rather than
# re-implementing kable's formatting.
report_kable_wrap_long_columns <- function(rendered, table, threshold = 40L, width_frac = 0.55) {
  wrap_idx <- which(vapply(seq_along(table), function(i) {
    col <- table[[i]]
    (is.character(col) || is.factor(col)) &&
      any(nchar(as.character(col)) > threshold, na.rm = TRUE)
  }, logical(1L)))
  if (!length(wrap_idx)) return(rendered)
  lines <- strsplit(rendered, "\n", fixed = TRUE)[[1L]]
  head_end <- which(lines == "\\endhead")[1L]
  foot_start <- which(lines == "\\bottomrule")[1L]
  if (is.na(head_end) || is.na(foot_start) || head_end >= foot_start - 1L) return(rendered)
  width_expr <- sprintf("%.2f\\textwidth", width_frac / length(wrap_idx))
  ncol <- length(table)
  for (i in seq(head_end + 1L, foot_start - 1L)) {
    line <- lines[[i]]
    if (!grepl("\\\\\\\\[ \t]*$", line)) next
    body <- sub("\\\\\\\\[ \t]*$", "", line)
    cells <- strsplit(body, " & ", fixed = TRUE)[[1L]]
    if (length(cells) != ncol) next
    for (j in wrap_idx) cells[[j]] <- sprintf("\\parbox[t]{%s}{%s}", width_expr, cells[[j]])
    lines[[i]] <- paste0(paste(cells, collapse = " & "), "\\\\")
  }
  paste(lines, collapse = "\n")
}

# \resizebox can perfectly, continuously scale a table down to exactly fit
# \textwidth -- but it can't wrap a longtable at all (resizebox measures one
# finished box; a longtable's whole point is breaking across an unknown
# number of pages, which can't be pre-measured as one box). Confirmed
# directly: a discrete font-size fallback alone (no resizebox) still let
# very wide tables (a real DAPC/PCA-scores-shaped 10-32 numeric-column
# table) overflow \textwidth even at \scriptsize, a real regression against
# the original \resizebox behaviour for exactly the common case (a table
# that fits on one page but has many columns) that behaviour was written
# for. So the choice is made per table, by \sbox-measuring a throwaway
# plain-tabular copy of the exact same (already wrapped) cell content: a
# table whose natural height already exceeds most of a page cannot use
# \resizebox regardless (it needs to paginate) and gets longtable with the
# coarser discrete-size fallback; everything else -- the large majority of
# real result tables -- keeps the original, exact-fit \resizebox behaviour,
# completely unchanged from before longtable existed here.
report_kable_render <- function(longtable_body) {
  lines <- strsplit(longtable_body, "\n", fixed = TRUE)[[1L]]
  tabular_lines <- lines[lines != "\\endhead"]
  # Located by content, not a fixed index -- kable()'s own output carries a
  # leading blank line before \begin{longtable}, which a fixed-position
  # substitution silently missed (confirmed directly: produced a
  # \begin{longtable}...\end{tabular} mismatch, a hard LaTeX compile error).
  begin_idx <- grep("^\\\\begin\\{longtable\\}", tabular_lines)[1L]
  end_idx <- grep("^\\\\end\\{longtable\\}$", tabular_lines)[1L]
  if (!is.na(begin_idx)) {
    tabular_lines[begin_idx] <- sub("^\\\\begin\\{longtable\\}", "\\\\begin{tabular}", tabular_lines[begin_idx])
  }
  if (!is.na(end_idx)) {
    tabular_lines[end_idx] <- sub("^\\\\end\\{longtable\\}$", "\\\\end{tabular}", tabular_lines[end_idx])
  }
  tabular_body <- paste(tabular_lines, collapse = "\n")
  # A raw-LaTeX line whose very first character is a bare "{" or "}" (not
  # attached to a preceding backslash command) is not recognized by
  # pandoc's raw-tex passthrough inside a results='asis' chunk -- confirmed
  # directly: it rendered as a literal, visible brace character in the
  # compiled PDF instead of functioning as TeX grouping. \begingroup/
  # \endgroup (both backslash commands, like every other line here) give
  # the same scoping without ever starting a line with a bare brace.
  paste0(
    "\\sbox{\\pgvcftablebox}{\\begingroup\n", tabular_body, "\n\\endgroup}\n",
    # \ht alone is only the box's height above its own reference point, not
    # its full visual extent -- confirmed directly on a real 80-row table,
    # \ht came in just under the threshold (531pt vs. a 533pt cutoff) while
    # \ht+\dp (1058pt) was unambiguously over it, sending an 80-row table
    # down the non-paginating \resizebox branch instead and silently
    # dropping every row past where it overflowed the page, the exact
    # defect this whole function exists to prevent. Every real caller of
    # this box (pandoc's own image-scaling macro included) uses \ht+\dp for
    # the same reason.
    "\\ifdim\\dimexpr\\ht\\pgvcftablebox+\\dp\\pgvcftablebox\\relax>0.82\\textheight\n",
    "\\ifdim\\wd\\pgvcftablebox>1.5\\textwidth\n\\def\\pgvcftablesize{\\scriptsize}\n",
    "\\else\\ifdim\\wd\\pgvcftablebox>1.15\\textwidth\n\\def\\pgvcftablesize{\\footnotesize}\n",
    "\\else\\ifdim\\wd\\pgvcftablebox>\\textwidth\n\\def\\pgvcftablesize{\\small}\n",
    "\\else\n\\def\\pgvcftablesize{\\normalsize}\n",
    "\\fi\\fi\\fi\n",
    "\\begingroup\\pgvcftablesize\n", longtable_body, "\n\\endgroup\n",
    "\\else\n",
    "\\ifdim\\wd\\pgvcftablebox>\\textwidth\n",
    "\\resizebox{\\textwidth}{!}{\\begingroup\n", tabular_body, "\n\\endgroup}\n",
    "\\else\n",
    "\\begingroup\n", tabular_body, "\n\\endgroup\n",
    "\\fi\n",
    "\\fi\n"
  )
}

report_kable <- function(table, digits = NULL) {
  # kable()'s default ("pipe") output is pandoc markdown, meant to be
  # converted by pandoc's own markdown-to-LaTeX pass -- fine standalone, but
  # NOT valid content inside raw LaTeX (which pandoc never re-processes for
  # embedded markdown table syntax). LaTeX output explicitly requests
  # format="latex" so kable() itself emits real longtable source, safe to
  # measure/wrap directly. longtable (not a plain, page-bound tabular) is
  # required so a table taller than one page paginates instead of silently
  # overflowing past the physical page and losing rows -- confirmed
  # directly on a real production report (a >100-row table's tail simply
  # never appeared anywhere in the rendered PDF).
  latex <- knitr::is_latex_output()
  args <- list(x = table, format = if (latex) "latex" else "pipe")
  if (!is.null(digits)) args$digits <- digits
  if (latex) args <- c(args, list(booktabs = TRUE, longtable = TRUE))
  rendered <- do.call(knitr::kable, args)
  if (!latex) {
    cat(rendered, sep = "\n")
    cat("\n\n")
    return(invisible(TRUE))
  }
  rendered <- report_kable_repeat_header(rendered)
  rendered <- report_kable_wrap_long_columns(rendered, table)
  cat(report_kable_render(rendered))
  cat("\n")
  invisible(TRUE)
}

report_heading <- function(title, level = 1L) {
  cat(strrep("#", level), " ", title, "\n\n", sep = "")
}

# A single-paragraph, data-independent explanation of what a section's test
# or statistic measures and what it does and doesn't support concluding --
# the same kind of framing wiki/Results-and-Interpretation.md gives each
# method, reused here so every rendered report carries it, not only the
# wiki. Emitted as a markdown blockquote: portable to both html_document
# (default Bootstrap already styles blockquote as an indented callout) and
# pdf_document (a LaTeX quote environment; report_pdf_preamble() below adds
# a left rule and muted color to match). `note` must be a single line (no
# embedded "\n") -- markdown blockquote syntax requires each line of a
# multi-line quote to carry its own leading "> ", which a raw embedded
# newline would not have, silently breaking the quote into a separate
# paragraph outside it.
report_note <- function(note) {
  if (is.null(note) || !nzchar(note)) return(invisible(FALSE))
  cat("> ", note, "\n\n", sep = "")
  invisible(TRUE)
}

# Groups the figure gallery's flat, numerically-ordered file list into the
# same named modules the table sections above already explain, purely by
# matching each figure's stem (report_figure_inventory()'s own caption
# source) against a fixed, ordered pattern catalog -- first match wins, so
# more specific patterns (e.g. the four per-backend ancestry-model families,
# which all otherwise share a "14_..._Q_K<k>" shape) are listed before their
# broader neighbours. Every stem pattern here is taken directly from the
# real `save_plot()`/`sprintf()` call sites across R/*.R, not guessed, so a
# renamed or newly added figure stem needs a matching catalog entry added
# here too -- an unmatched stem is not an error, it simply gets no heading
# or note (the same bare figure output this gallery already had before this
# catalog existed), so a gap here never blocks the report from rendering.
report_figure_family_catalog <- function() {
  list(
    list(pattern = "^0[1-4]_", heading = "Quality control", note = paste0(
      "Sample and SNP counts, and the distributions behind the MAF and ",
      "missingness thresholds, through each stage of filtering. A final ",
      "retained count alone cannot show which rule removed what."
    )),
    list(pattern = "^(05_sample_heterozygosity|06_population_diversity|19_HWE_pvalues|44_allelic_richness)", heading = "Genetic diversity", note = paste0(
      "Observed/expected heterozygosity, Hardy-Weinberg exact-test ",
      "p-values, and rarefied allelic richness by population. A significant ",
      "HWE deviation, or an imbalance between observed and expected ",
      "heterozygosity, has many non-error causes (technical artifacts, ",
      "substructure, inbreeding, selection) and is descriptive, not an ",
      "automatic exclusion criterion."
    )),
    list(pattern = "^(06b_PCA_Tracy_Widom|07b?_PCA_PC|17_PCA_loadings|18_PCA_loadings)", heading = "Principal component analysis", note = paste0(
      "Unsupervised ordination of the genotype matrix; each retained axis ",
      "is a direction of maximal variance, not a population. Separation ",
      "along an axis can reflect population history, relatedness, batch ",
      "effects, geography, or sampling design -- corroborate with other ",
      "structure-detecting results before drawing conclusions. Axis sign is ",
      "arbitrary and can flip without changing the underlying solution."
    )),
    list(pattern = "^(08_IBS_MDS|09_IBS_heatmap|52_IBS_tree)", heading = "Identity-by-state and individual relationships", note = paste0(
      "Identity-by-state (IBS) is a simpler, symmetric similarity measure ",
      "than kinship below: the fraction of alleles shared between every ",
      "pair of samples, with no explicit relatedness model behind it. These ",
      "views describe overall similarity structure, not directional ",
      "ancestry or a specific relatedness degree."
    )),
    list(pattern = "^55_ML_tree", heading = "Maximum-likelihood phylogenetic tree", note = paste0(
      "A genuine maximum-likelihood alternative to the neighbour-joining ",
      "tree above: a configurable nucleotide substitution model ",
      "(analyses.ml_tree.model, default GTR), gamma-distributed among-site ",
      "rate variation, and a Lewis (2001) ascertainment-bias correction for ",
      "SNP-only data (no invariant sites are ever recorded in a VCF), ",
      "jointly optimized with the topology. Bootstrap support at each node ",
      "uses the same resampling procedure and interpretation as the NJ tree."
    )),
    list(pattern = "^(10_pairwise_FST|51_population_specific_fst)", heading = "Population differentiation (FST)", note = paste0(
      "Weir-Cockerham FST, pairwise and population-specific (beta). FST ",
      "depends on population definitions, sample size, marker ",
      "ascertainment, missingness, and the genomic region analyzed -- state ",
      "the estimator explicitly whenever a value here is reported elsewhere."
    )),
    list(pattern = "^53_population_tree", heading = "Population genetic distance and tree", note = paste0(
      "Nei's (1972) standard genetic distance between populations, computed ",
      "from allele frequencies -- a population-level counterpart to the ",
      "individual-level IBS view above. The neighbour-joining tree carries ",
      "locus-resampling bootstrap support at each internal node ",
      "(Felsenstein 1985)."
    )),
    list(pattern = "^(11_DAPC_K|12_DAPC_cluster_number_selection|12b_DAPC_xval|14_DAPC_membership|15_DAPC_loadings|16_DAPC_loadings)", heading = "Discriminant analysis of principal components (DAPC)", note = paste0(
      "For a chosen number of clusters K, DAPC maximizes between-group ",
      "separation given the genotype data. Because the same data both ",
      "defines the groups and is then shown separated by them, strong ",
      "visual separation is not independent confirmation that those groups ",
      "are real populations -- corroborate with a model-based ancestry ",
      "method or kinship before drawing that conclusion."
    )),
    list(pattern = "^12_isolation_by_distance", heading = "Mantel test and isolation by distance", note = paste0(
      "Tests whether genetic distance increases with geographic distance ",
      "(Mantel test, with a partial-Mantel variant controlling for ",
      "population membership when metadata allows; Smouse, Long & Sokal ",
      "1986). A significant association does not establish a causal ",
      "spatial process and can be sensitive to autocorrelation or ",
      "clustered sampling."
    )),
    list(pattern = "^(13_ADMIXTURE_CV|13b_ADMIXTURE_cluster_number_selection|14_ADMIXTURE_Q)", heading = "ADMIXTURE ancestry model", note = paste0(
      "K is a model index for the best-fitting number of mixture ",
      "components, not a literal count of ancestral populations -- colored ",
      "cluster components need independent evidence (geography, pedigree, ",
      "known biology) before being read as historical populations."
    )),
    list(pattern = "^(13c_sNMF_cluster_number_selection|14_sNMF_Q)", heading = "sNMF ancestry model", note = paste0(
      "A sparse non-negative matrix factorization fit, independent of ",
      "ADMIXTURE/fastStructure's likelihood model. K is a model index, not ",
      "a literal count of ancestral populations; the three ancestry ",
      "backends are run independently and are not averaged or otherwise ",
      "reconciled by default -- differing consensus K values across ",
      "backends illustrate computational agreement, or its absence, not a ",
      "contradiction to resolve."
    )),
    list(pattern = "^(13d_fastStructure_cluster_number_selection|14_fastStructure_Q)", heading = "fastStructure ancestry model", note = paste0(
      "Fits the same underlying admixture model as ADMIXTURE via a ",
      "different optimizer. Agreement between the two on both K and ",
      "per-sample cluster membership is stronger evidence of real signal ",
      "than either result alone; K itself remains a model index, not a ",
      "literal count of ancestral populations."
    )),
    list(pattern = "^20_private_alleles", heading = "Private alleles", note = paste0(
      "Alleles observed in exactly one retained population. Presence here ",
      "describes allele-frequency structure; it is not, by itself, ",
      "evidence of adaptive significance or of any particular demographic ",
      "history."
    )),
    list(pattern = "^(21_kinship_heatmap|22_kinship_IBS0)", heading = "Kinship", note = paste0(
      "Pairwise relatedness (KING-robust kinship, Manichaikul et al. ",
      "2010), specifically robust to population stratification. This is a ",
      "continuous relatedness screen, not a certified pedigree or an ",
      "exact-genotype-identity test -- see multilocus genotype diversity ",
      "below for that stricter, independent check."
    )),
    list(pattern = "^(23_ROH|24b?_ROH)", heading = "Runs of homozygosity", note = paste0(
      "Runs of homozygosity (`bcftools roh`, an HMM-based method; ",
      "Narasimhan et al. 2016) -- a per-sample autozygosity/inbreeding ",
      "signal, distinct from both the population-level inbreeding ",
      "coefficient and pairwise kinship. `FROH` is scaled to the genomic ",
      "footprint actually covered by the analyzed variants, not the whole ",
      "genome -- never compare FROH across analyses covering different ",
      "genomic spans."
    )),
    list(pattern = "^(25_genome_scan_FST|26b?_genome_scan)", heading = "Genome scans", note = paste0(
      "Windowed FST, diversity, and Tajima's D along physical position -- a ",
      "descriptive ranking, not a significance test: no permutation or null ",
      "distribution is computed. A high-FST window is a candidate worth ",
      "further investigation, not a confirmed selection signal, and ",
      "Tajima's D is systematically biased upward by MAF filtering, which ",
      "removes rare variants before this scan ever sees them."
    )),
    list(pattern = "^43_LD_decay", heading = "Linkage disequilibrium decay", note = paste0(
      "Mean pairwise genotypic correlation (r-squared) between SNPs, ",
      "binned by physical distance, computed on the unpruned marker set -- ",
      "the LD-pruned set used elsewhere would systematically understate how ",
      "far real LD extends."
    )),
    list(pattern = "^45_Ne_LD", heading = "LD-based effective population size", note = paste0(
      "Contemporary effective population size per population, estimated ",
      "from linkage disequilibrium between cross-chromosome, effectively ",
      "unlinked SNP pairs (Waples 2006; Waples & Do 2008). A single point ",
      "estimate carries real sampling variance -- read it as ",
      "order-of-magnitude, not exact."
    )),
    list(pattern = "^47_population_assignment", heading = "Population assignment test", note = paste0(
      "A frequency-based self-assignment test (Paetkau et al. 1995, 2004; ",
      "Rannala & Mountain 1997 leave-one-out correction): each sample's ",
      "genotype is scored against every population's own allele ",
      "frequencies and assigned to whichever maximizes that likelihood. A ",
      "sample whose assigned population differs from its recorded label is ",
      "a candidate migrant or a metadata question, not an automatic ",
      "correction of the record."
    )),
    list(pattern = "^48_site_frequency_spectrum", heading = "Site frequency spectrum and bottleneck screen", note = paste0(
      "Bins each population's segregating loci by folded minor allele ",
      "frequency; the accompanying mode-shift test (Luikart & Cornuet ",
      "1998) flags a possible recent-bottleneck signature. This is a ",
      "qualitative screen, not a confirmed bottleneck, and is sensitive to ",
      "MAF filtering -- interpret it alongside the QC thresholds used for ",
      "this run. It is not assessed for a population with fewer called ",
      "samples than frequency classes, whose lowest class cannot hold a ",
      "locus."
    )),
    list(pattern = "^50_spatial_autocorrelation", heading = "Spatial autocorrelation", note = paste0(
      "Bins sample pairs into geographic-distance classes and reports a ",
      "spatial-autocorrelation coefficient per class (Smouse & Peakall ",
      "1999), with a permutation-based null envelope -- a ",
      "distance-resolved complement to the single overall Mantel r above, ",
      "showing whether an isolation-by-distance signal concentrates at ",
      "particular spatial scales. The first class includes co-located ",
      "pairs (distance 0). With population-level-only coordinates it ",
      "holds every within-site pair and the correlogram contrasts same ",
      "site with different sites rather than resolving fine-scale ",
      "structure; intermediate classes can be empty."
    )),
    list(pattern = "^59_pcadapt_manhattan", heading = "pcadapt outlier scan", note = paste0(
      "A genuine per-locus statistical outlier test for local adaptation ",
      "(Luu et al. 2016), computed on the full unpruned marker set and ",
      "needing no population metadata. In strongly structured samples a ",
      "large fraction of loci can appear significant from ordinary ",
      "genome-wide drift alone, not necessarily localized selection -- ",
      "check whether significant loci cluster into a handful of linked ",
      "windows before over-interpreting the count."
    )),
    list(pattern = "^27_sex_check", heading = "Sex check", note = paste0(
      "Genetic sex inferred from X-chromosome heterozygosity and ",
      "Y-chromosome call rate, compared against any reported `sex` ",
      "metadata. When both signals are available and agree, that is a ",
      "high-confidence call; when they confidently disagree the combined ",
      "status is `discordant` -- real, informative evidence, not noise to ",
      "average away."
    )),
    list(pattern = "^(58_genotype_accumulation_curve|58b_MSN_network)", heading = "Multilocus genotype (MLG) and clonal diversity", note = paste0(
      "Multilocus genotype identity and clonal-diversity statistics ",
      "(`poppr`; Kamvar, Tabima & Grunwald 2014), computed on the full, ",
      "unpruned QC-passing marker set for maximum discriminating power. ",
      "Because it requires identity at every locus in a large marker ",
      "panel, ordinary genotyping error can make even truly related or ",
      "clonal individuals fail this exact match -- a sparse network or a ",
      "flat accumulation curve does not by itself contradict a ",
      "relatedness-based lineage signal found elsewhere in this report."
    )),
    list(pattern = "^60_sexbias_AIc", heading = "Sex-biased dispersal test", note = paste0(
      "Tests whether one recorded sex disperses more than the other, using ",
      "each individual's assignment index (AIc; Favre et al. 1997) -- how ",
      "strongly their genotype matches their own recorded population, ",
      "corrected for sample size (Goudet, Perrin & Waser 2002). This test ",
      "was designed for single-species, dispersal-focused sampling with ",
      "reproductive-age individuals genotyped at natal versus breeding ",
      "location; a null result from data collected for another purpose is ",
      "expected, not necessarily evidence against sex-biased dispersal."
    ))
  )
}

report_figure_family <- function(stem, catalog) {
  for (entry in catalog) {
    if (grepl(entry$pattern, stem)) return(entry)
  }
  NULL
}

report_table_section <- function(title, table, digits = NULL, level = 1L, note = NULL) {
  # A genuinely zero-column table (write_chromosome_results() returns a bare
  # data.table() when no chromosome met chromosome_min_snps) is not NULL,
  # but knitr::kable(format="latex") on it emits \begin{tabular}{} -- an
  # empty column spec that is invalid LaTeX and hard-crashes the PDF
  # compile. length() on a data.frame/data.table is its column count.
  if (is.null(table) || !length(table)) return(invisible(FALSE))
  report_heading(title, level)
  report_note(note)
  report_kable(table, digits)
  invisible(TRUE)
}
```

# Executive summary

This `r toupper(params$report_format)` file is a portable, human-readable
analysis report. Figures are embedded directly in the file. The HTML version
can be opened in a standard web browser, while the PDF version is optimized for
compact exchange, printing, and email. The accompanying `analysis_results.rds`
file is a reproducibility archive for
R users; it is not required to read this report.

`r if (!is.null(r$package_version)) sprintf("Generated with **popgenVCF v%s**.", r$package_version)`

The analysis retained **`r nrow(r$metadata)` samples** from **`r data.table::uniqueN(r$metadata$population)` populations**, with **`r length(r$qc_snps)` QC-passing SNPs** and **`r length(r$final_snps)` LD-pruned SNPs**.

```{r analysis-sections, results='asis'}
pipeline_notices <- NULL
if (!is.null(r$messages) && nrow(r$messages)) {
  pipeline_notices <- r$messages[r$messages$level %in% c("WARNING", "INFO"), c("stage", "level", "message")]
  if (!nrow(pipeline_notices)) pipeline_notices <- NULL
}
report_table_section("Pipeline notices", pipeline_notices)
if (!is.null(r$fst$global) && length(r$fst$global) &&
    is.finite(r$fst$global[[1L]])) {
  cat(sprintf(
    "The global Weir-Cockerham $F_{ST}$ estimate was **%.4f**.\n\n",
    r$fst$global[[1L]]
  ))
}
report_table_section(
  "Quality control", r$qc$sequential, digits = 2,
  note = paste0(
    "Sample and SNP counts retained after each filtering stage, in sequence -- ",
    "a final count alone cannot show which rule removed what. With ",
    "qc.autosome_only, markers set aside for the sex-check module have ",
    "their own \"After autosome restriction\" row rather than being ",
    "counted as LD-pruning removals. Filtering ",
    "thresholds should be set before looking at population patterns, not ",
    "fitted afterward to produce a preferred result."
  )
)
report_table_section(
  "Genetic diversity", r$diversity$population, digits = 4,
  note = paste0(
    "Per-population expected/observed heterozygosity and the inbreeding ",
    "coefficient F. A negative or positive F does not identify a cause by ",
    "itself -- technical artifacts, population substructure, inbreeding, and ",
    "selection can all produce a similar signature; treat this table as a ",
    "starting point for further investigation, not a conclusion."
  )
)
private_alleles <- NULL
if (!is.null(r$diversity$locus)) {
  pa <- r$diversity$locus[
    !is.na(r$diversity$locus$private_allele) & r$diversity$locus$private_allele != "none",
    c("population", "snp_id", "chromosome", "position", "private_allele",
      "alternate_allele_count", "reference_allele_count")
  ]
  if (nrow(pa)) private_alleles <- head(pa, 20)
}
report_table_section(
  "Private alleles (up to 20 shown; see 32_private_alleles.tsv for the complete list)",
  private_alleles,
  note = paste0(
    "Alleles observed in exactly one retained population. Presence here ",
    "describes allele-frequency structure; it is not, by itself, evidence ",
    "of adaptive significance or of any particular demographic history."
  )
)
report_table_section(
  "Principal component analysis",
  if (!is.null(r$pca$scores)) head(r$pca$scores, 20) else NULL,
  digits = 4,
  note = paste0(
    "Unsupervised ordination of the genotype matrix; each retained axis is a ",
    "direction of maximal variance, not a population. Separation along an ",
    "axis can reflect population history, relatedness, batch effects, ",
    "geography, or sampling design -- corroborate with other ",
    "structure-detecting results (kinship, clustering, FST) before drawing ",
    "conclusions. Axis sign is arbitrary and can flip without changing the ",
    "underlying solution."
  )
)
pca_loadings_top <- NULL
if (!is.null(r$pca$loadings) && nrow(r$pca$loadings)) {
  pca_loadings_top <- head(r$pca$loadings[order(-r$pca$loadings$magnitude), ], 20)
}
report_table_section(
  "PCA SNP loadings (top 20 by |loading|; see 31_PCA_loadings.tsv for the complete top-N list)",
  pca_loadings_top, digits = 4,
  note = paste0(
    "Ranks SNPs by how strongly they correlate with each retained PCA axis, ",
    "by magnitude rather than raw value. A large loading identifies a marker ",
    "associated with an axis, not a causal or functionally validated ",
    "variant -- treat it as a lead for further investigation, not a conclusion."
  )
)
report_table_section(
  "Population differentiation", r$fst$long, digits = 4,
  note = paste0(
    "Weir-Cockerham FST, global and pairwise, with Wright's (1931) Nm ",
    "gene-flow estimate alongside it as a direct transform of the same ",
    "value -- treat Nm as a rescaled FST, not a measured number of ",
    "migrants per generation: the formula assumes an equilibrium ",
    "island model (equal deme sizes, symmetric migration, no selection) ",
    "that real populations violate, and it inherits every caveat of the ",
    "FST it was derived from. FST depends on population definitions, ",
    "sample size, marker ascertainment, missingness, and the genomic ",
    "region analyzed -- state the estimator explicitly whenever a value ",
    "from this table is reported elsewhere."
  )
)
population_distance_table <- NULL
if (!is.null(r$population_tree$distance) && nrow(r$population_tree$distance)) {
  population_distance_table <- as.data.frame(r$population_tree$distance)
  population_distance_table <- cbind(population = rownames(population_distance_table), population_distance_table)
  rownames(population_distance_table) <- NULL
}
report_table_section(
  "Nei's standard genetic distance between populations (see 46_population_genetic_distance.tsv; a neighbour-joining tree with bootstrap support at each node, alongside the individual-level IBS tree, is written and rendered as a figure when at least three populations are present -- see 52_IBS_tree and 53_population_tree)",
  population_distance_table, digits = 4,
  note = paste0(
    "Nei's (1972) standard genetic distance between populations, computed ",
    "from allele frequencies -- a population-level counterpart to the ",
    "individual-level IBS and kinship distances used elsewhere in this ",
    "report. The accompanying neighbour-joining tree carries ",
    "locus-resampling bootstrap support at each internal node (Felsenstein ",
    "1985)."
  )
)
report_table_section(
  "Genome scan FST outliers (top 20 windows by FST; see 39_genome_scan_fst.tsv for the complete list)",
  r$genome_scan$outliers, digits = 4,
  note = paste0(
    "A descriptive ranking of the highest-FST genomic windows -- not a ",
    "significance test, since no permutation or null distribution is ",
    "computed. A high-FST window is a candidate worth further ",
    "investigation, not a confirmed selection signal; always check a ",
    "window's SNP count before treating its estimate as meaningful."
  )
)
pcadapt_top <- NULL
if (!is.null(r$pcadapt$table)) {
  sig <- r$pcadapt$table[!is.na(r$pcadapt$table$q_value) & r$pcadapt$table$q_value < 0.05, ]
  if (nrow(sig)) pcadapt_top <- head(sig[order(sig$q_value), ], 20)
}
report_table_section(
  "pcadapt outlier scan (top 20 significant loci by q-value; see 59_pcadapt_outliers.tsv for the complete results and 59b_pcadapt_significant_outliers.tsv for the complete significant list)",
  pcadapt_top, digits = 4,
  note = paste0(
    "A genuine per-locus statistical outlier test for local adaptation (Luu ",
    "et al. 2016), distinct from the descriptive genome-scan ranking above: ",
    "each locus's genotypes are regressed on the retained PCA axes and ",
    "tested against a chi-squared null, with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR ",
    "correction across all tested loci. It needs no population metadata. In ",
    "strongly structured samples a large fraction of loci can appear ",
    "significant from ordinary genome-wide drift alone, not necessarily ",
    "localized selection -- check the genomic inflation factor and whether ",
    "significant loci cluster into a handful of linked windows before ",
    "over-interpreting the count."
  )
)
report_table_section(
  "Linkage disequilibrium decay (mean r-squared by physical distance bin; see 43_LD_decay.tsv for the complete list)",
  r$ld_decay$binned, digits = 4,
  note = paste0(
    "Mean pairwise genotypic correlation (r-squared) between SNPs, binned ",
    "by physical distance, computed on the unpruned marker set -- the ",
    "LD-pruned set used elsewhere in this report would systematically ",
    "understate how far real LD extends. A real decay curve falls off ",
    "within a bounded distance rather than staying flat or noisy across the ",
    "full range."
  )
)
report_table_section(
  "LD-based effective population size (per population; see 45_Ne_LD.tsv for full diagnostics)",
  r$ne_ld, digits = 4,
  note = paste0(
    "Contemporary effective population size per population, estimated from ",
    "linkage disequilibrium between cross-chromosome, effectively unlinked ",
    "SNP pairs (Waples 2006; Waples & Do 2008). A single point estimate ",
    "carries real sampling variance -- read it as order-of-magnitude, not ",
    "exact. `Inf` means no drift signal was detectable above sampling ",
    "noise (a real, informative result); `NA` with status ",
    "`below_formula_domain` means the implied size falls outside the ",
    "estimator's valid range, i.e. smaller still."
  )
)
report_table_section(
  "Bottleneck mode-shift screen (per population; see 48_site_frequency_spectrum.tsv for the full spectrum)",
  r$bottleneck$summary, digits = 3,
  note = paste0(
    "The modal class of each population's folded site frequency spectrum ",
    "(Luikart & Cornuet 1998). Under mutation-drift equilibrium the lowest ",
    "class holds the most loci; a mode in a higher class is a possible ",
    "recent-bottleneck signature -- a qualitative screen, not a p-value, ",
    "and sensitive to the MAF filter. `mode_shifted` is `NA` with status ",
    "`too_few_samples` where a population has fewer called samples than ",
    "frequency classes: the smallest attainable minor allele frequency is ",
    "1/(2n), so its lowest class cannot hold a locus at all."
  )
)
close_relatives <- NULL
if (!is.null(r$kinship$close_relatives) && nrow(r$kinship$close_relatives)) {
  close_relatives <- head(r$kinship$close_relatives, 20)
}
report_table_section(
  "Close relatives (up to 20 shown; see 36_close_relatives.tsv for the complete list)",
  close_relatives, digits = 4,
  note = paste0(
    "Pairwise relatedness (KING-robust kinship, Manichaikul et al. 2010), ",
    "specifically robust to population stratification. This is a ",
    "continuous relatedness screen, not a certified pedigree or an ",
    "exact-genotype-identity test -- see the multilocus genotype table ",
    "below for that stricter, independent check."
  )
)
sex_check_top <- NULL
if (!is.null(r$sex_check$table) && nrow(r$sex_check$table)) {
  sc <- r$sex_check$table
  if ("status" %in% names(sc) && any(!is.na(sc$status))) {
    priority <- match(sc$status, c("discordant", "mismatch", "ambiguous", "not_reported", "match"))
    priority[is.na(priority)] <- 5L
    sc <- sc[order(priority, sc$x_heterozygosity_F), ]
  } else {
    sc <- sc[order(sc$x_heterozygosity_F), ]
  }
  sex_check_top <- head(sc, 20)
}
report_table_section(
  "Sex check (reported vs inferred sex from X-chromosome heterozygosity and Y-chromosome call rate; up to 20 shown, discordant and ambiguous calls first; see 42_sex_check.tsv for the complete list)",
  sex_check_top, digits = 4,
  note = paste0(
    "Genetic sex inferred from X-chromosome heterozygosity and Y-chromosome ",
    "call rate, compared against any reported `sex` metadata. When both ",
    "signals are available and agree, that is a high-confidence call; when ",
    "they confidently disagree the combined status is `discordant` -- real, ",
    "informative evidence worth following up, not noise to average away."
  )
)
roh_top <- NULL
if (!is.null(r$roh$sample_summary) && nrow(r$roh$sample_summary)) {
  roh_top <- head(r$roh$sample_summary[order(-r$roh$sample_summary$froh), ], 20)
}
report_table_section(
  "Runs of homozygosity (highest FROH samples, up to 20 shown; see 38_ROH_sample_summary.tsv for the complete list)",
  roh_top, digits = 4,
  note = paste0(
    "Runs of homozygosity (`bcftools roh`, an HMM-based method; Narasimhan ",
    "et al. 2016) -- a per-sample autozygosity/inbreeding signal, distinct ",
    "from both the population-level inbreeding coefficient and the pairwise ",
    "kinship above. `FROH` is scaled to the genomic footprint actually ",
    "covered by the analyzed variants, not the whole genome -- never ",
    "compare FROH values across analyses covering different genomic spans."
  )
)
report_table_section(
  "Discriminant analysis of principal components",
  r$dapc$diagnostics,
  digits = 4,
  note = paste0(
    "For a chosen number of clusters K, DAPC maximizes between-group ",
    "separation given the genotype data. Because the same data both ",
    "defines the groups and is then shown separated by them, strong visual ",
    "separation is not independent confirmation that those groups are real ",
    "populations -- corroborate with a model-based ancestry method or ",
    "kinship before drawing that conclusion."
  )
)
dapc_loadings_top <- NULL
if (!is.null(r$dapc$models) && length(r$dapc$models)) {
  loading_tables <- lapply(names(r$dapc$models), function(k) {
    loadings <- r$dapc$models[[k]]$loadings
    if (is.null(loadings) || !nrow(loadings)) return(NULL)
    cbind(K = k, loadings[, c("axis", "snp_id", "chromosome", "position", "contribution")])
  })
  loading_tables <- loading_tables[!vapply(loading_tables, is.null, logical(1L))]
  if (length(loading_tables)) {
    combined <- do.call(rbind, loading_tables)
    dapc_loadings_top <- head(combined[order(-combined$contribution), ], 20)
  }
}
report_table_section(
  "DAPC SNP loadings (top 20 by contribution across all K; see 22f_DAPC_loadings_K<k>.tsv for the complete per-K top-N lists)",
  dapc_loadings_top, digits = 4,
  note = paste0(
    "Ranks SNPs by their contribution to each DAPC discriminant axis, ",
    "across all fitted K. As with PCA loadings, a large contribution ",
    "identifies a marker associated with a discriminant axis, not a causal ",
    "variant."
  )
)
if (!is.null(r$amova)) {
  report_heading("Analysis of molecular variance")
  report_note(paste0(
    "Partitions total genetic variance hierarchically among the supplied ",
    "grouping (Excoffier et al. 1992), with each component tested by ",
    "permutation. Phi-population-total is the same quantity as FST computed ",
    "through variance partitioning rather than an allele-frequency ",
    "estimator. A negative variance component is a real, expected estimator ",
    "artifact -- typically driven by within-group relatedness exceeding the ",
    "model's assumptions -- not an error to discard."
  ))
  if (!is.null(r$amova$components)) {
    report_kable(r$amova$components, digits = 4)
  }
  if (!is.null(r$amova$phi)) {
    report_kable(r$amova$phi, digits = 4)
  }
}
report_table_section(
  "Multilocus genotype (MLG) and clonal diversity",
  r$clonality$summary, digits = 4,
  note = paste0(
    "Multilocus genotype identity and clonal-diversity statistics ",
    "(`poppr`; Kamvar, Tabima & Grunwald 2014), computed on the full, ",
    "unpruned QC-passing marker set -- deliberately more loci than the ",
    "LD-pruned set used for kinship, for maximum discriminating power. The ",
    "standardized index of association (rbarD; Agapow & Burt 2001) near ",
    "zero indicates strong linkage among loci, consistent with clonal ",
    "reproduction; it does not, alone, prove it."
  )
)
clonality_groups <- NULL
if (!is.null(r$clonality$groups) && nrow(r$clonality$groups)) {
  clonality_groups <- head(r$clonality$groups, 20)
}
report_table_section(
  "Samples sharing an identical multilocus genotype (up to 20 groups shown; see 57_MLG_groups.tsv for the complete list)",
  clonality_groups,
  note = paste0(
    "Samples sharing an identical multilocus genotype at every analyzed ",
    "locus -- a strict, exact-match test, deliberately stricter than the ",
    "continuous relatedness threshold used for close relatives above. ",
    "Because it requires identity at every locus in a large marker panel, ",
    "ordinary genotyping error can make even truly related or clonal ",
    "individuals fail this exact match; a small or empty result here does ",
    "not by itself contradict a relatedness-based lineage signal found ",
    "elsewhere in this report."
  )
)
if (!is.null(r$sexbias)) {
  report_heading("Sex-biased dispersal test")
  report_note(paste0(
    "Tests whether one recorded sex disperses more than the other, using ",
    "each individual's assignment index (AIc; Favre et al. 1997) -- how ",
    "strongly their genotype matches their own recorded population, ",
    "corrected for sample size (Goudet, Perrin & Waser 2002). This test was ",
    "designed for single-species, dispersal-focused sampling with ",
    "reproductive-age individuals genotyped at natal versus breeding ",
    "location; a null result from data collected for another purpose is ",
    "expected, not necessarily evidence against sex-biased dispersal."
  ))
  cat(sprintf(
    "%s test: statistic = %.3f, p = %.4f (n = %d female, %d male%s). See 60_sexbias_AIc_by_sample.tsv for per-sample assignment indices.\n\n",
    r$sexbias$test, r$sexbias$statistic, r$sexbias$p_value,
    r$sexbias$n_female, r$sexbias$n_male,
    if (r$sexbias$permutations > 0) sprintf(", %d permutations", r$sexbias$permutations) else ""
  ))
}
report_table_section(
  "Mantel test and isolation by distance", r$ibd$summary, digits = 4,
  note = paste0(
    "Tests whether genetic distance increases with geographic distance ",
    "(Mantel test, with a partial-Mantel variant controlling for population ",
    "membership when metadata allows; Smouse, Long & Sokal 1986). A ",
    "significant association does not establish a causal spatial process ",
    "and can be sensitive to autocorrelation or clustered sampling -- ",
    "especially when the same populations are also compared by FST or PCA ",
    "elsewhere in this report."
  )
)
report_table_section(
  "Admixture-model cross-validation", r$admixture_cv, digits = 6,
  note = paste0(
    "Cross-validation error by K for the ADMIXTURE ancestry model. K is a ",
    "model index for the best-fitting number of mixture components, not a ",
    "literal count of ancestral populations -- colored cluster components ",
    "need independent evidence (geography, pedigree, known biology) before ",
    "being read as historical populations."
  )
)
report_table_section(
  "Chromosome-specific results", r$chromosome_summary, digits = 4,
  note = paste0(
    "Repeats FST and a short PCA separately for each chromosome with ",
    "enough QC-passing markers (below analyses.chromosome_min_snps is ",
    "silently excluded), so a signal concentrated on one chromosome can ",
    "be distinguished from a genome-wide pattern. Read a standout value ",
    "as a marker-density or chromosome-length question first (fewer SNPs ",
    "give noisier per-chromosome estimates) and a biology question only ",
    "after comparing its qc_snps/ld_snps counts against the others."
  )
)
```

# Figure gallery

The gallery contains one version of every analysis figure. The HTML report
prefers browser-friendly SVG or PNG files, with large PNGs downsampled to
screen resolution. The PDF report prefers the compact vector PDF source for
each figure. Original full-resolution files remain available in the sibling
`figures/` directory.

```{r figure-gallery, results='asis'}
figure_family_catalog <- report_figure_family_catalog()
current_figure_family <- NULL
report_figure_family_heading <- function(stem) {
  family <- report_figure_family(stem, figure_family_catalog)
  key <- if (is.null(family)) NA_character_ else family$heading
  if (identical(key, current_figure_family)) return(invisible(FALSE))
  current_figure_family <<- key
  if (is.null(family)) return(invisible(FALSE))
  report_heading(family$heading, level = 2L)
  report_note(family$note)
  invisible(TRUE)
}
if (is.null(report_figures) || !nrow(report_figures)) {
  cat("No figure files were found. Configure `output.figure_formats` to include `pdf`, `png`, or `svg`, then regenerate the report.\n")
} else if (knitr::is_html_output()) {
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(report_figures))) {
    figure <- report_figures[i, , drop = FALSE]
    report_figure_family_heading(figure$stem[[1L]])
    caption <- html_escape(figure$caption[[1L]])
    filename <- html_escape(basename(figure$path[[1L]]))
    uri <- knitr::image_uri(figure$path[[1L]])
    if (identical(figure$format[[1L]], "pdf")) {
      cat(sprintf(
        paste0(
          '<figure style="margin:2em 0">',
          '<figcaption><strong>%s</strong><br><small>%s</small></figcaption>',
          '<p><a href="%s" target="_blank">Open the embedded PDF figure</a></p>',
          '</figure>\n'
        ),
        caption, filename, uri
      ))
    } else {
      cat(sprintf(
        paste0(
          '<figure style="margin:2em 0">',
          '<img src="%s" alt="%s" loading="lazy" ',
          'style="display:block;max-width:100%%;height:auto;margin:auto">',
          '<figcaption style="text-align:center;margin-top:0.5em">',
          '<strong>%s</strong><br><small>%s</small></figcaption>',
          '</figure>\n'
        ),
        uri, caption, caption, filename
      ))
    }
  }
} else {
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(report_figures))) {
    figure <- report_figures[i, , drop = FALSE]
    report_figure_family_heading(figure$stem[[1L]])
    caption <- figure$caption[[1L]]
    path <- gsub(" ", "%20", figure$path[[1L]], fixed = TRUE)
    cat(sprintf(
      "![%s](%s){width=95%%}\n\n\\newpage\n\n",
      caption, path
    ))
  }
}
```

# Reproducibility

This report was generated from the serialized pipeline result object. Exact input hashes, settings, package versions, and stage runtimes are stored alongside the report.

```{r reproducibility-sections, results='asis'}
if (!is.null(r$dapc) && "replicate_max_rmse" %in% names(r$dapc$diagnostics)) {
  report_table_section(
    "Population-structure reproducibility",
    r$dapc$diagnostics[, c("K", "assignment_accuracy", "replicate_max_rmse")],
    digits = 4, level = 2L
  )
}
if (!is.null(r$faststructure$runs)) {
  # executable/log_file/q_file are long, space-free absolute paths -- unlike
  # every other reproducibility table here (DAPC, sNMF), which already
  # select only meaningful columns, this one previously dumped the full raw
  # runs table: those path columns cannot wrap at a word boundary (no
  # spaces to break on) and overflowed the table, reported directly against
  # a real production report. executable is also identical on every row.
  # Full paths remain available in analysis_results.rds regardless.
  faststructure_runs <- r$faststructure$runs[
    , intersect(c("K", "exit_status", "marginal_likelihood"), names(r$faststructure$runs)),
    with = FALSE
  ]
  report_table_section("fastStructure", faststructure_runs, digits = 4, level = 2L)
}
if (!is.null(r$snmf$diagnostics)) {
  report_table_section(
    "Sparse non-negative matrix factorization",
    r$snmf$diagnostics,
    digits = 6, level = 2L
  )
}
```
